title: I Had An Accident in San Francisco

direction.promise: Surviving the futuristic danger of a solo trip does not protect you from ordinary life.
direction.want: Enjoy San Francisco, experience the sights and driverless tech, and catch the flight home safely.
direction.choice: Take an ordinary human-driven airport cab after safely surviving a driverless Waymo.
direction.consequence: The cab driver slams the brakes on the highway and gets rear-ended five minutes from SFO.
direction.payoff: The futuristic robot car was harmless, but a five-minute human taxi ride ended in police reports and tears.

beats.thought: Surviving the impossible only makes the ordinary more dangerous.
A solo trip is liberating and exciting.
beats.intent: Ground the story in her genuine enthusiasm.

beats.thought: I packed every possible activity into this trip.
The Apple event felt completely futuristic.
The Golden Gate Bridge was breathtaking.
Riding a Waymo sounded like a wild idea.
A ghost is literally steering this vehicle.
I genuinely believed today was my last day on earth.
beats.intent: Reach the comedic peak of Waymo terror.

beats.thought: I survived the robot car unscathed.
beats.intent: Set up the false sense of security.

beats.thought: Time to head to the airport in a boring normal taxi.

script.text: Wait. Do you know that feeling where you survive something genuinely terrifying... and then get completely taken out by the most normal thing on Earth?
Okay, so I went on a solo trip to San Francisco. First time traveling completely by myself.
And honestly? It was amazing. I walked twenty thousand steps a day and did literally every tourist activity.
I went to the Apple event that happened recently. Felt like I was living in the year 2040.
Then I visited the Golden Gate Bridge. Look at this view. Absolutely gorgeous.
And then... I rode a Waymo. For context, it is a completely autonomous, driverless car.
No driver in the front seat. The steering wheel was just turning by itself like a ghost.
I was clutching the back seat the entire time thinking: this is it. This is my final day.
But we arrived safely. Flawless ride. I thought the dangerous part of the trip was officially behind me.
Trip is over. I am heading to the airport in a completely normal human-driven taxi.
Five minutes. We are literally five minutes away from the departure terminal.
We are cruising down the highway at high speed, and out of nowhere, my driver slams the brakes.
We stop in time. But the car right behind us? Definitely did not.
They plowed straight into our rear bumper. I was sitting in the back seat. My soul left my body.
Two minutes later, highway patrol pulls up. Flashing red and blue lights everywhere.
Officers walking around with flashlights, taking statements, inspecting the crushed bumper...
And instead of being a calm, rational adult... I just completely broke down and started crying.
Survive the futuristic driverless robot taxi without a scratch? Easy. Take a five-minute airport cab? Total disaster.
